claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Approximately 1–2 at.% of one unspecified base element will be replaced by W.
The W substitution will produce finely dispersed W-rich precipitates.
The W addition and associated precipitates will refine the alloy grains.
The proposed microstructural changes will improve intergranular cohesion.
Improved intergranular cohesion and microstructural refinement will increase resistance to crack initiation and propagation.
The W-induced microstructural modification will not significantly disturb the caloric phase transformation.
The phase transformation is responsible for the alloy's caloric response.
W substitution will produce a statistically significant improvement in compressive strength relative to the unchanged alloy.
The improved compressive strength will approach levels reported for previously reinforced MM′X systems.
The caloric response of the W-modified alloy will remain within approximately 10% of the unchanged alloy's response.
The proposed comparison requires identical processing and thermal histories for the W-modified and unchanged samples.
Mechanical and caloric evaluations will use matched applied-field, pressure, temperature, and compressive-loading regimes.
The hypothesis is intended to apply near the caloric phase-transition temperature during applied-field and pressure-field operation and compressive loading.
